title: Кража сыра с плесенью  (The Stolen Blue Cheese)

segments.t: Back at Claude Monet, habitual kitchen pilferer Senya is calmly drinking chamomile tea when sous-chef Katya storms in. Someone has stolen expensive blue cheese from the walk-in fridge, and to protect himself, Senya smoothly convinces Katya that newcomer Denis is the kitchen thief.
Сеня, что ты там сейчас пьёшь?
Я тут тёплую ромашку для горла пью.
Ребята, кто-то украл сыр с плесенью!
Ещё утром я видела его в холодильнике.
Вот негодяи, совсем совесть потеряли!
Вы знаете, какая у нас недостача?
Дай мне ромашки, я горло сорвала.
Извини, Катя, в чашке почти не осталось.
Обрати лучше внимание на нашего новенького.
До его прихода такой недостачи не было.
Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!
Спасибо, Сеня, я за ним прослежу.
Let's look closely at how Senya deflects suspicion onto Denis in the kitchen.
Сеня, что ты там сейчас пьёшь?
'Senya, what are you drinking over there right now?' By wondering what Katya drinking over there right now is, Fedya presses Katya for a straight answer.
Я тут тёплую ромашку для горла пью.
'I am drinking warm chamomile here for my throat.' Mentioning that he is drinking warm chamomile here for his throat moves the talk in a new direction.
Ребята, кто-то украл сыр с плесенью!

'Guys, someone stole the blue cheese!' Katya insists that someone stole the blue cheese, leaving Fedya no room to argue. Russian puts the key word right up front so her emotion lands on the first beat.
Ещё утром я видела его в холодильнике.
'Just this morning I saw it in the refrigerator.' Because just this morning she saw it in the refrigerator, Katya treats the matter as settled.
Вот негодяи, совсем совесть потеряли!

'What scoundrels, they have completely lost their conscience!' Senya declares that what scoundrels they have completely lost their conscience as the tension in the room peaks. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Вы знаете, какая у нас недостача?

'Do you know what a shortage we have?' Checking whether Fedya knows what a shortage they have cuts straight through the tension between Katya and Fedya. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Дай мне ромашки, я горло сорвала.
'Give me some chamomile, I strained my throat.' Noting that Fedya should give her some chamomile she strained her throat keeps Katya's side of the story simple and clear.
Извини, Катя, в чашке почти не осталось.
'Sorry, Katya, there is almost none left in the cup.' Pointing out that there is almost none left in the cup gives Fedya a sobering reality check.
Обрати лучше внимание на нашего новенького.
'You had better pay attention to our newcomer.' Senya mentions that Fedya had better pay attention to their newcomer so Fedya sees what is at stake.
До его прихода такой недостачи не было.
'Before his arrival there was no such shortage.' Realizing that before his arrival there was no such shortage changes how Senya handles the situation.
Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!

'As soon as he appeared, groceries immediately started disappearing!' Saying that as soon as he appeared groceries immediately started disappearing is how Senya takes charge of the moment. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Спасибо, Сеня, я за ним прослежу.

'Thank you, Senya, I will keep an eye on him.' Even though she will keep an eye on him, Katya keeps a steady face in front of Fedya. Now listen to the complete conversation about the missing cheese at natural speed.

Convinced by Senya's tip, Katya begins watching Denis's every move around the kitchen. Next, German tries to win Vika's heart with the mystery flower bouquet. See you next time!
До встречи!
